name: RTS Action Replay
description: Capture OBS replay-buffer clips and play them through a [[blue:Streamer.bot]] controlled browser overlay.\nUses its own [[blue:fully featured catalog]], with search capabilities. Over [[blue:39 commands]] for complete control through chat on all supported platforms.\nThe Settings interface allows customisation of [[blue:colours]], [[blue:layout]] and [[blue:behaviour]].

website.footerLabel: Part of The Road to Somewhere.

experience.title: Turn OBS replay clips into an interactive on-stream replay player.
experience.text: RTS Action Replay connects OBS Replay Buffer captures, [[blue:Streamer.bot]] and a remote browser overlay so saved clips can be loaded and controlled without a separate web server.

features.title: Supports Twitch, YouTube and Kick
features.text: Full support for [[purple:Twitch]],  [[red:YouTube]], and  [[green:Kick]] (via kickbot or kick). Capture clips directly from the platform's chat, and catalog them. Full cross-platform capabilities, with automatic platform branding depending on which platform initiated the command.

features.title: Complete Branding control
features.text: Customise the [[white:Brand Colours]], [[white:Logo]], and [[white:fonts]] to fit your stream design. [[blue:4 Design presets]] to choose from. Choose different presets for different platforms.

features.title: Full catalog with search, rating and leaderboards
features.text: Complete [[blue:catalog]] of all your clips, with full searching by [[white:date]], [[white:creator]], and [[white:rating]]. Leaderboards keep track of top clippers and clip requestors. Full [[blue:playlist]] functionality to queue multiple requested clips.

features.title: Remote or local overlay
features.text: A complete, functioning [[blue:overlay]] to perform all the actions you need, with a [[white:dev mode]] for easy configuring and testing of the extension.

features.title: Complete layout control with full animation
features.text: Complete control with our [[blue:positioning system]] lets you position the [[white:Player]], [[white:Search Panels]], and [[white:Overlay Messages]] wherever you want, Create [[blue:entry/exit animations]] for them with ease.

features.title: Include complete set of Chat commands
features.text: Chat commands for everything: [[white:clipping]], [[white:Queuing]], [[white:Catalog Searching]], [[white:Playlist control]], and [[white:video control]].

requirements: [[blue:Streamer.bot]] with its WebSocket and HTTP servers enabled.
RtsUI.dll for the extension settings interface.

setup.title: Get Action Replay running.
setup.intro: Import the [[blue:Streamer.bot]] actions, enable them, configure OBS Replay Buffer and the local HTTP file mapping, add the overlay to OBS, then test Action Replay.

steps.title: Import the extension into [[blue:Streamer.bot]]
steps.description: Open [[blue:Streamer.bot]] and use Import to paste the supplied import string, or download the latest import file and import it into [[blue:Streamer.bot]].

substeps.title: Copy the import string
substeps.text: Look above for Action Import, click the Copy Import button, then paste the import code into [[blue:Streamer.bot's]] Import dialog.

images.alt: The RTS extension import code with an arrow pointing to the import code button

substeps.title: Open Import
substeps.text: Select Import from the [[blue:Streamer.bot]] toolbar.

images.alt: Streamer.bot import screen showing the RTS extension import code

substeps.title: Paste the import code
substeps.text: Paste the supplied import string into the Import String box, then select Import.

images.alt: Streamer.bot import confirmation dialog

substeps.title: Confirm the import
substeps.text: Review the actions being imported, then select Import to continue.

images.alt: Streamer.bot second import confirmation dialog

steps.title: Enable the imported actions
steps.description: Enable the imported RTS Action Replay actions and commands so the extension can respond to events and chat commands.

substeps.title: Enable the extension actions
substeps.text: Enable the imported RTS Action Replay actions in [[blue:Streamer.bot]].

images.alt: Streamer.bot imported RTS actions being enabled

substeps.title: Check and Enable the commands
substeps.text: Confirm the imported RTS Action Replay commands are present and enabled where required.

images.alt: Streamer.bot commands showing the imported RTS Action Replay commands

steps.title: Enable OBS Replay Buffer
steps.description: If you want to enable capturing of local files created by the OBS Replay Buffer, choose the folder where the replay files are saved.

substeps.title: Enable Replay Buffer
substeps.text: In OBS, open Settings > Output and enable Replay Buffer.

images.alt: Configure OBS Replay Buffer

substeps.title: Choose the replay folder
substeps.text: Configure OBS to save replay files to a folder that [[blue:Streamer.bot]] can access. You will use this same folder when configuring the HTTP Server mapping and RTS Action Replay settings.

images.alt: Configure OBS Replay Buffer

steps.title: Configure the [[blue:Streamer.bot]] HTTP Server
steps.description: The hosted RTS overlay cannot read files directly from your computer. [[blue:Streamer.bot's]] HTTP Server provides the local URL that the overlay uses to load replay video files.

substeps.title: Enable the HTTP Server
substeps.text: In [[blue:Streamer.bot]], open the Servers or Web Server settings and enable the HTTP Server. Keep note of the HTTP port.

images.alt: Setting up the HTTP Server in Streamer.bot

substeps.title: Add file mappings to the HTTP server
substeps.text: Create a file or directory mapping for the OBS Replay Buffer folder. Use a simple URL path such as [[code:replays]] and point it to the same local folder where OBS saves replay files.\nIf you want to save Twitch and Kick clips locally, add a mapping for those too. The mapping should point to the folder you set up in the extension settings for Twitch and Kick.

images.alt: Mappings section of the HTTP server settings

substeps.title: Keep the HTTP server available
substeps.text: Leave the [[blue:Streamer.bot]] HTTP Server running while using Action Replay. The overlay uses this service to request the local replay video. It's recommended to turn on the toggle at the top of the HTTP settings to have the HTTP server auto-start on launch.

steps.title: Enable the [[blue:Streamer.bot]] WebSocket
steps.description: The hosted overlay uses the [[blue:Streamer.bot]] WebSocket to receive Action Replay events and commands.

substeps.title: Enable the WebSocket Server
substeps.text: In [[blue:Streamer.bot]], open the WebSocket Server settings and enable the server. Keep the configured port available to the overlay.

images.alt: Streamer.bot WebSocket Server Settings

substeps.title: Keep WebSocket access available
substeps.text: The [[blue:Streamer.bot]] WebSocket Server must remain running while the Action Replay overlay is in use. It's recommended to turn on the toggle at the top of the WebSocket settings to have the WebSocket server auto-start on launch.

steps.title: Add the Action Replay overlay to OBS
steps.description: Add the Action Replay hosted overlay as an OBS Browser Source, or use the supplied local overlay files.

substeps.title: Copy the Overlay URL
substeps.text: Look above in the Quick Access section and click the Copy Overlay URL button. This copies the overlay URL to your clipboard for use in OBS.

images.alt: RTS Copy Overlay URL button screenshot

substeps.title: Create a browser source
substeps.text: Add a Browser Source to an existing or newly created scene in OBS.

images.alt: OBS add a new browser source dialog

substeps.title: Configure the browser source
substeps.text: Paste the Overlay URL you just copied into the URL field, then set the width and height to 1920x1080 or another 16:9 size. The Action Replay overlay uses a 1920x1080 coordinate system. Enable Refresh browser when scene becomes active if required by your scene setup.

images.alt: OBS browser source settings dialog

steps.title: Configure RTS Action Replay Settings
steps.description: Open the RTS Action Replay settings and configure the extension.

substeps.title: Open the settings dialog
substeps.text: In the [[blue:Streamer.bot]] Actions panel, look for RTS Action Replay settings action to open the extension settings. The settings are fully documented below in [[yellow:Action Replay Documentation]]

images.alt: Streamer.bot commands showing the imported RTS Action Replay commands

substeps.title: Automatic installation of RtsUI.dll
substeps.text: If you do not have the DLL installed, the extension can download and place it in your [[blue:Streamer.bot]] installation directory. If you do not see the install prompt, it may be hiding behind another window. Check your taskbar for a [[blue:Streamer.bot]] dialog and bring it to the front.

substeps.title: Automatic updating of RtsUI.dll
substeps.text: If the extension requires an updated version, it can ask whether you want to download and install the latest version. If you do not see the update prompt, it may be hiding behind another window. Check your taskbar for a [[blue:Streamer.bot]] dialog and bring it to the front.

steps.title: Test Action Replay Setup and Configuration
steps.description: Test and set up the Extension using the overlay's built-in development mode.

substeps.title: Put the overlay into dev mode
substeps.text: Copy the [[overlay:Overlay URL]], open it in a browser, and add [[muted:?dev=true]] at the end.\n\nThis will put the overlay into dev mode, where you can test and preview the extension's features and settings.

images.alt: Send the configuration to the dev overlay

substeps.title: Send the current config to the overlay
substeps.text: In the Test tab of the extension's settings, you can click the Send Configuration to Overlay button. Once this is done, all the presets will be sent to the overlay and can be previewed.

images.alt: Send the configuration to the dev overlay

substeps.title: Use the test harness to preview your current settings.
substeps.text: The Testing tab of the settings allows you to send various actions to the overlay so you can preview your changes easily.\n\nAfter changing an option in the test settings, click save before initiating a test.

documentation.title: Action Replay Settings Guide
documentation.intro: There are a large number of settings that enable you to configure how the extension behaves and looks.\nThis documentation guide aims to walk you through what each setting does, allowing you to tailor the extension to your specific needs.

steps.title: Local Capture
steps.description: [[blue:Streamer.bot]] can be set up to watch a folder for new media.\nThis is particularly useful for OBS (or other capture/streaming software) when captures via its replay buffer are saved to a folder on your computer. [[blue:Streamer.bot]] picks this up and adds the file to the catalog.\n[[blue:Streamer.bot's]] HTTP Service maps the folder and serves the file to the overlay when requested.

images.alt: Screenshot of settings for Local Capture

settings.title: Replay Folder
settings.description: Browse to the folder where you have set up OBS (or other streaming software) to save its Replay Buffer files to.\nTwitch and Kick downloads use separate folders and are configured in their own sections.

settings.title: Replay File Types
settings.description: File extensions accepted when scanning or registering files from the Replay Folder. Separate multiple extensions with commas, for example [[code:.mp4, .mkv]].

settings.title: HTTP Mapping
settings.description: URL path used in the local replay URL. It must match the [[blue:Streamer.bot]] HTTP server mapping you set up in the installion step [[yellow:04]].

settings.title: HTTP Port
settings.description: Port used in the local replay URL. It must match Streamer.bot's HTTP server port.

images.alt: screenshot of settings for Replay Defaults

settings.title: Replay Title Template
settings.description: Generates the title of a newly added OBS replay. Available variables are [[code:%replayName%]], [[code:%replayDate%]] and [[code:%replayTime%]]. A manually supplied title bypasses the template.

substeps.title: Local Capture Handling

images.alt: Screenshot for Local Capture Handling

settings.title: Auto-add Saved Replays (OBS Capture)
settings.description: Adds each newly saved OBS replay to the Catalog. It also becomes available to Recent Clips through the Catalog's recent history.

settings.title: Auto-play OBS Captures
settings.description: Adds a newly saved OBS replay to the playback queue for playback.

notes: When automatic registration is disabled, existing replay files can still be registered with Add Replay or Scan Replays.
commands: [[muted:!save-replay, !clip-local <title>]] - *This command sends a raw request to OBS Studio and saves the replay buffer; it is not set up to work with other streaming software right now.

steps.title: Twitch
steps.description: Configure how [[purple:Twitch clips]] are acquired and made available to the player.

substeps.title: Twitch Clips

images.alt: Screenshot for Twitch Settings

settings.title: Twitch Clip Playback
settings.description: Use the Twitch URL, download locally, or support both methods.\nIn Both mode, a local copy is preferred, and Twitch is the fallback.

settings.title: Twitch Clip Folder
settings.description: Folder used for downloaded Twitch clips. It must be separate from the OBS Replay Folder.

settings.title: Twitch HTTP Mapping
settings.description: URL path used by [[blue:Streamer.bot]] to serve downloaded Twitch clips. The shared HTTP Port is configured under Local Capture / OBS.

settings.title: Clip Duration
settings.description: Default duration used by Twitch clip commands when no duration is supplied.

notes: The allowed Twitch clip duration is 5-60 seconds. A duration supplied with the command overrides the setting within that range.

steps.title: YouTube
steps.description: Configure timestamp-based clips from the current monitored [[red:YouTube]] broadcast.

substeps.title: YouTube Clips

images.alt: Screenshot for YouTube Clips settings

settings.title: Clip Duration
settings.description: Default duration used by [[red:YouTube]] clip commands when no duration is supplied.

notes: The allowed duration is 5-60 seconds. Action Replay uses the current broadcast and its monitored start time to calculate the clip timestamp.

steps.title: Kick
steps.description: Configure how [[green:Kick]] clips are acquired and made available to the player.

images.alt: Screenshot for Kick Clip settings

settings.title: Kick Clip Playback
settings.description: Use the [[green:Kick]] URL, download locally, or support both methods. In Both mode, a local copy is preferred, and direct [[green:Kick]] playback is the fallback.

settings.title: Kick Clip Folder
settings.description: Folder used for downloaded [[green:Kick]] clips. It must be separate from the OBS Replay Folder.

settings.title: Kick HTTP Mapping
settings.description: URL path used by [[blue:Streamer.bot]] to serve downloaded [[green:Kick]] clips. The shared HTTP Port is configured under Local Capture / OBS.

steps.title: Player
steps.description: Control how replays start and how playback controls and player styling are presented.

images.alt: Screenshot for Playback settings

settings.title: Show Controls
settings.description: Displays the Play/Pause control and interactive playback progress bar.

settings.title: Show Progress Bar
settings.description: Displays the interactive playback progress bar.

settings.title: Default Playback Speed
settings.description: Playback speed used when a replay is loaded; normal playback speed is 1. Range from 0.25 to 2.0.

settings.title: Show Visibility
settings.description: Controls when the playback speed indicator is displayed.

substeps.title: Player Appearance

images.alt: Screenshot for Player Appearance settings

settings.title: Frame Colour Source
settings.description: Uses a Custom, Branding Primary or Branding Secondary colour for the player frame.

settings.title: Frame Colour
settings.description: Custom frame colour when Frame Colour Source is Custom.

settings.title: Control Colour Source
settings.description: Uses a Custom, Branding Primary or Branding Secondary colour for the Play/Pause control and progress bar.

settings.title: Control Colour
settings.description: Custom control colour when Control Colour Source is Custom.

settings.title: Border Glow
settings.description: Adds a branded glow around the player border.

settings.title: Border Width
settings.description: Player border width in pixels.

settings.title: Corner Radius
settings.description: Player corner radius in pixels.

notes: Colours support opacity using the alpha slider in the colour picker.\nChange Player Branding to Clip Source is configured later under Player Behaviour. When enabled, it can override the player frame and control branding with the active source branding option.

steps.title: Catalog
steps.description: The Catalog is the persistent replay library. Recent Clips and Last Played are different views/history derived from replay data, while the Playlist is the live playback queue.

images.alt: Screenshot for catalog settings

settings.title: Maximum Recent Clips
settings.description: Maximum number of entries shown in Recent Clips and retained in Last Played history. Older Catalog entries remain available.

settings.title: Maximum Catalog Results
settings.description: Maximum number of results shown per Catalog/search page. The [[code:--amount]] option can request a different page size up to this limit.

settings.title: Persist Playlist Across Restarts
settings.description: Keeps the current Playlist queue when [[blue:Streamer.bot]] restarts. Active playback and pause state are not persisted.

steps.title: Branding Presets
steps.description: Define reusable colours, typography and branding identity used by Player, Panel, Clapperboard and Message presentation.

substeps.title: Brand Preset Settings
substeps.text: There are 5 branding presets pre-configured: [[white:default]], [[yellow:RTS]], [[purple:Twitch]], [[red:YouTube]], and [[green:Kick]]. They can be changed, but not deleted.\nYou can create and delete extra presets as you need, and they will be available for use throughout the settings.

images.alt: Screenshot for Branding Presets settings

settings.title: Preset Name
settings.description: Display name used in settings and selection lists.

settings.title: Source Platform
settings.description: Optional [[purple:Twitch]], [[green:Kick]], or [[red:YouTube]] association.\n This Branding Preset will be used when the [[yellow:Use Source Branding option]] is turned on.\ne.g. If [[purple:Twitch]] is set as the source platform, this branding preset will be used to style requests initiating from [[purple:Twitch]].

settings.title: Primary Colour
settings.description: Primary branding colour.

settings.title: Secondary Colour
settings.description: Secondary branding colour.

settings.title: Player Title Colour
settings.description: Replay title text colour.

settings.title: Player Prefix / Suffix Colour
settings.description: Decorative title prefix/suffix colour.

settings.title: Panel Text Colour
settings.description: Panel title/list text colour.

settings.title: Panel List Shadow Colour
settings.description: Panel list shadow colour.

settings.title: Font
settings.description: Google Font used by player titles, panel titles and branding.

settings.title: Font Size
settings.description: Font size used by player and panel titles.

settings.title: Logo URL
settings.description: HTTPS URL of the branding logo.

settings.title: Fallback Text
settings.description: Text used when the branding logo cannot be loaded.

settings.title: Brand Label
settings.description: Label displayed with the logo or fallback text.

steps.title: Design Presets
steps.description: Define the visual treatment used by Player, Panel, and Message presentation.\nThere are 2 configurable presets [[yellow:Broadcast]] and [[yellow:Cut]], plus two non-configurable presets [[yellow:Cinematic]] and [[yellow:Minimal]]

substeps.title: Broadcast
substeps.text: Provides an animated chevron treatment.

images.alt: Screenshot for Broadcast Design Preset settings

settings.title: Background Source
settings.description: The background colour to use for panels,and messages. Options: RTS Dark Blue background, Branding Secondary Colour, or Custom Colour

settings.title: Background Colour
settings.description: The colour will be used if Custom is set for Background Source

settings.title: Chevron Height
settings.description: How tall the chevrons will appear. 1 - 89

settings.title: Randomise Height
settings.description: The height for each chevron will be randomised as it is generated, between 1 and the Chevron Height setting

settings.title: Chevron Width
settings.description: How wide the chevrons will appear. 1-300

settings.title: Randomise Width
settings.description: The width for each chevron will be randomised as it is generated. between 0 and the Chevron Width setting

settings.title: Chevron Spacing
settings.description: How much space between each chevron. 0-200

settings.title: Randomise Spacing
settings.description: The space between each chevron will be randomised as it is generated. between 0 and the Chevron Space setting

settings.title: Chevron Speed
settings.description: How fast the chevrons move horizontally from left to right. 10-500

substeps.title: Cut
substeps.text: Provides an animated block/bar treatment.

images.alt: Screenshot for Cut Design Preset settings

settings.title: Background Source
settings.description: The background colour to use for panels, and messages. Options: RTS Dark Blue background, Branding Secondary Colour, or Custom Colour

settings.title: Background Colour
settings.description: The colour will be used if Custom is set for Background Source

settings.title: Block Width
settings.description: How wide the blocks will appear. 1 - 600

settings.title: Randomise Height
settings.description: The height for each chevron will be randomised as it is generated, between 1 and the Block Width setting

settings.title: Bar Height
settings.description: How tall the blocks will appear. 1-50

steps.title: Title Presets
steps.text: Define how replay titles are positioned, decorated, and animated in the Player.

substeps.title: Title Presets
substeps.text: Define how replay titles are positioned, decorated, and animated in the Player. The default preset can be changed, but not deleted.\n*DO NOT RENAME THE DEFAULT PRESET!!!

images.alt: Screenshot for the Title Presets settings

settings.title: Preset Name
settings.description: Display name for the preset.

settings.title: Decoration Position
settings.description: Places the decoration before or after the title.

settings.title: Title Position
settings.description: Places the title at the top or bottom of the player.

settings.title: Decoration
settings.description: Text displayed as the title prefix/suffix.

settings.title: Animation
settings.description:
Title entrance/exit animation. There are 3 options:
Left to Right - Slides in from the left to the right: Slides out from the right to the left
Right to Left - Slides in from the right to the left : Slides out from the left to the right
Slide Up/Down - Slides up from the bottom and back down, or slides down from the top and back up, depending on whether the title is positioned at the top or the bottom. : Slides out from Right to Left

settings.title: Show Delay
settings.description: Delay before the title is shown, in milliseconds.

settings.title: Display Duration
settings.description: Time the title remains displayed, in milliseconds.

settings.title: Animation Duration
settings.description: Duration of the title animation, in milliseconds.

steps.title: Positions
steps.description: Define reusable Player, Panel, Message, and Clapperboard positions in the shared 1920x1080 overlay coordinate space.

substeps.title: Panel and Message Positions
substeps.text: Panel and Messages can have their Width, Height, and Corner Radius set. After changing these options, save and exit settings, then reopen settings before editing the positions.\nPositions are used in animation presets for displaying the Panels/Messages.

images.alt: Screenshot for Panel Positions settings

settings.title: Width
settings.description: Width of Panel/Message in pixels.

settings.title: Height
settings.description: Height of Panel/Message in pixels.

settings.title: Corner Radius
settings.description: Corner Radius of Panel/Message in pixels.

settings.title: Edit Positions
settings.description: Opens the RTS Position Editor (See Position Editor below)

substeps.title: Player Positions
substeps.text: Saved positions used by Player Animation and playback.

settings.title: Edit Positions
settings.description: Opens the RTS Position Editor (See Position Editor below)

substeps.title: Clapperboard Positions
substeps.text: Saved positions used by Clapperboard Animation and playback.

settings.title: Edit Positions
settings.description: Opens the RTS Position Editor (See Position Editor below)

substeps.title: RTS Position Editor
substeps.text: The [[yellow:RTS Position Editor]] allows you to place the Player, Panels, Messages, and Clapperboard anywhere on your display;\n you can place elements on and off screen then use the animation presets to show and hide elements however you choose.\n The position editor is based on a 16:9 resolution and works on 1080p and 1440 resolutions. All four position editors support saved transforms, including scale, X/Y/Z position, and X/Y/Z rotation. Animation Profiles reference these saved positions, so changing a saved position affects every profile that uses it.

images.alt: Screenshot of the RTS - Position Editor

settings.title: Position Presets
settings.description: The left-hand column lists the presets that have been created. The [[code:Full Screen]] is a default preset and cannot be edited. Presets you create will appear here and will be available for the [[yellow:animation editor]] (see below)

settings.title: Position Titles and Tags
settings.description: When creating a position you can set the title and a tag, the tag is used when using !set-pos command to position the player, currently it is not possible to set the position of Panels, Messages, or the Clapperboard on the fly.

settings.title: Positioning X, Y, Z
settings.description: Allows positioning of the element on the X, Y, and Z axis, 0 is centered. You can move the element left using - values and right using positive values. Z moves the element towards you (positive, e.g. 100) or away from you (negative e.g -100) in 3d space.

settings.title: Transform X, Y, Z
settings.description: Allows rotating of the element on the X, Y, and Z axis, 0 is centered. You can rotate the element left using - values and right using positive values. Z rotates the element left (negative e.g -100) or right (positive, e.g. 100) on a flat plane

settings.title: Scale X, Y
settings.description: Allows resizing of the elements' X and Y values; setting to 0 will effectively hide the element completely

settings.title: Availiable Buttons
settings.description:
Add Position - Adds a new position preset.
Duplicate - Duplicates the selected Position Preset.
Delete - Deletes the selected Preset.
Preview Position- Sends the current position to the dev overlay so you can see exactly where it will appear on the overlay.
Hide Preview - I have no clue what this was for or what it does...

settings.title: Save, Close and Cancel
settings.description: They do what they say; make sure you click Save before previewing a position. Always save and exit, unless you want to lose your changes.

steps.title: Animation Profiles
steps.description: Animation Profiles are created to allow complete configuration of how your elements appear and disappear.\nThere are 4 animation profile tabs one each for the [[yellow:Player]], [[yellow:Panel]], [[yellow:Message]] and [[yellow:Clapperboard]]. The Animation system works the same for all elements. There is a default Animation profile for each element that cannot be deleted. More presets can be created for each element as needed.

substeps.title: Animation Sequences
substeps.text: Each Animation Profile has a [[yellow:Start Sequence]] and an [[yellow:End Sequence]]. The Start Sequence determines how the element appears; the End Sequence determines how it disappears.

images.alt: Screenshot for Animation Profiles

substeps.title: Start Sequence
substeps.text: A sequence is created from 1 or more positions defined in the elements [[yellow:Position Editor]]; only the positions for the current element will be shown, i.e., player positions cannot be used in Panel Sequences

images.alt: Screenshot for Animation Sequence Editor

settings.title: The First item in a Start sequence
settings.description: The first row determines the start position of the animation.\nIt is best to use a position where the element's width and height are set to 0, or an off-screen position.\nThe first position should alway have its duration and delay set to 0 as there is nothing for it to transistion from.

settings.title: Adding items to a sequence
settings.description: Click Add Row to add a new step in the sequence, the animation engine will use the rows setting and transition from the last item to smoothly transition to the next item.

settings.title: Position
settings.description: Select the position you want to transition to

settings.title: Duration
settings.description: The duration for the transition in milliseconds (1000ms = 1 second).

settings.title: Easing
settings.description: How you want the transition animation to run; easing affects the speed of the transition at its start and end. There are 4 easing settings to choose from.

settings.title: Delay
settings.description: How long to wait before starting the next item in the sequence.

settings.title: When the sequence ends
settings.description: Once the sequence is complete, the element will remain in its current position until its end sequence is triggered.\nFor Messages, Panels, and the Clapperboard, this will be the duration they are set to be displayed for; for the player, the end sequence will start when the last queued video has finished playing or the player is hiddden manually.

settings.title: End Sequence
settings.description: The end sequence operates the same way as a start sequence, except it animates from the current position of the element to the first element in the sequence and then continues each step of the sequence. Position, Duration, Easing, and delay are all taken into account for every row added.

steps.title: Player Behaviour
steps.description: The player Behaviour tab allows you to congigure how the player looks and behaves on each platform, there are 4 Create profiles for each platform: [[blue:OBS]], [[purple:Twitch]], [[red:YouTube]], and [[green:Kick]].\nThe Create profiles determine how the player looks when a clip is created on that platform.

substeps.title: Use Source Platform Branding
substeps.text: When this is on, the player will use the branding preset associated with the platform that created the clip, if a matching preset exists. Otherwise it will default to using the Branding set in the Play Replay setting (see below).\nWhen it is Off, the player will use the Branding Preset set in the Create setting for that platform.

images.alt: Screenshot for Use Source Platform Branding

substeps.title: Create [[blue:OBS]], [[purple:Twitch]], [[red:YouTube]], and [[green:Kick]] settings
substeps.text: Each platform can have its own Animation Profile, Design Preset, Title Preset, and Branding Preset.\nThe Create settings determine how the player looks when a clip is created and played from that platform.

images.alt: Screenshot for Player Behaviour Create settings

settings.title: Branding Preset
settings.description: Selects the Branding Preset to be used when a clip is created on the associated platform.

settings.title: Design Preset
settings.description: Selects the Design Preset to be used when a clip is created on the associated platform.

settings.title: Title Preset
settings.description: Selects the Title Preset to be used when a clip is created on the associated platform.

settings.title: Animation Profile
settings.description: Selects the Animation Profile to be used when a clip is created on the associated platform.

substeps.title: Play - Replay settings
substeps.text: The Play settings determine how the player looks when a clip is played from the [[yellow:Playlist]], [[yellow:Recent Clips]], or [[yellow:Last Played]].\nThe Branding Preset, Design Preset, Title Preset, and Animation Profile can be set independently of the Create settings.

images.alt: Screenshot for Use Source Platform Branding for playback

settings.title: Change Player Branding to Clip Source

substeps.text: Replay lifecycle notifications are configured under Replays, Playlist and Updates.

images.alt: Documentation screenshot placeholder for Replay Messages

settings.title: Replay Created
settings.description: Replay saved: %replayTitle%.

settings.title: Replay Played
settings.description: Play

settings.title: Replay Queued
settings.description: Replay queued: %replayTitle%.

settings.title: Replay Removed
settings.description: Replay removed: %replayTitle%.

settings.title: Playlist Cleared
settings.description: Playlist cleared: %clearedCount% waiting item(s) removed.

settings.title: Playlist Cleared All
settings.description: Playlist completely cleared: %clearedCount% item(s) removed.

settings.title: Replay Rated
settings.description: Rated %replayTitle% %replayRating%/5 (average %averageRating%/5).

settings.title: Replay Renamed
settings.description: Replay #%replayNumber% renamed from %oldTitle% to %newTitle%.

settings.title: Replay Deleted
settings.description: Replay deleted: %replayTitle%.

notes: Each event has message text and a Chat toggle. Events that support overlay output also have an Overlay toggle.
Replay Created uses the separate Clapperboard presentation when Use Clapperboard is enabled. The other overlay-capable lifecycle events use the Message presentation.
Overlay messages are queued centrally. Chat messages are sent immediately. An overlay message is considered finished only when its exit animation completes.
Replay Queued is generated only when the Playlist already contained an item before the new replay was added.

substeps.title: Import Settings
substeps.text: Import selected RTS Action Replay settings from a JSON file.

images.alt: Documentation screenshot placeholder for Import Settings

notes: The Import dialog controls which configuration areas, profiles and Catalog data are included and handles duplicate profiles.

substeps.title: Export Settings
substeps.text: Export the complete RTS Action Replay configuration to a JSON file.

images.alt: Documentation screenshot placeholder for Export Settings

notes: Export includes the configuration snapshot and supported global settings.

substeps.title: Factory Reset
substeps.text: Restore RTS Action Replay configuration to its built-in defaults.

images.alt: Documentation screenshot placeholder for Factory Reset

notes: Factory Reset preserves the Catalog and play history. Configuration globals are reset and required defaults are recreated.

substeps.text: Send Configuration to Overlay sends the complete current Action Replay configuration to the overlay for configuration-sync testing.

settings.title: Test Video

settings.title: Test Panel

settings.title: Test Clapperboard
settings.description: Shows the Clapperboard for the first Catalog replay using the current Clapperboard presentation settings.

images.alt: Documentation screenshot placeholder for Messages

settings.title: Message Type
settings.description: Selects the lifecycle message simulated by Test Message.

settings.title: Test Source
settings.description: Selects either the current Message settings or the selected Design and Branding overrides.

settings.title: Message Design
settings.description: When Test Source is Override, selects the presentation design used for the test.

settings.title: Message Branding
settings.description: When Test Source is Override, selects the presentation branding used for the test.

settings.title: Test Message
settings.description: Shows the selected message using the first Catalog replay. Chat output follows the selected Test Origin.

commands.title: Add Existing Replay
commands.description: Add one existing OBS replay file from the configured Replay Folder to the Catalog. If no title is supplied, the Replay Title Template is used. Existing Catalog entries are not added again.

commands.title: Search By Creator
commands.description: Search for replays by creator.

commands.title: Search By Date
commands.description: Search for replays from a date period. Supported forms include today, this week, last week, this year, last year, year, month and month year.

commands.title: Delete Clip
commands.description: Delete Catalog entries from the current result set. Multiple current-page results can be supplied as comma-separated numbers. The physical media file is not deleted.

commands.title: First Page
commands.description: Return to the first page of the current Catalog/search results.

commands.title: Last Page
commands.description: Jump to the last page of the current Catalog/search results.

commands.title: Most Views
commands.description: List replays ordered by playback count. Only replays with at least one recorded play are included.

commands.title: Next Page
commands.description: Move to the next page of the current Catalog/search results.

commands.title: Previous Page
commands.description: Move to the previous page of the current Catalog/search results.

commands.title: Purge
commands.description: Remove Catalog entries whose replay media can no longer be resolved. It does not delete physical files.

commands.title: Rate Replay
commands.description: Rate the replay currently playing. Rating is 1 to 5 and is stored per user.

commands.title: Search
commands.description: Search the Catalog by text. With no search text, returns the Catalog without a text filter.

commands.title: Show Current Search Page
commands.description: Show the current page of the current Catalog/search results.

commands.title: Search Top Rated
commands.description: List replays by rating. 0 is unrated; 1-4 select average rating bands 1.0-4.9; 5 selects a 5.0 average. Without a rating, rated replays are returned ordered by average rating.

commands.title: Leaderboard - Creator
commands.description: Show the creator leaderboard.

commands.title: Name Replay
commands.description: Give a Catalog replay a custom title. Custom titles must be unique, ignoring case. The physical video file is not renamed.

commands.title: Play History
commands.description: Play an item from the Last Played history.

commands.title: List Recent
commands.description: Show recently captured or added replays. This is different from Last Played.

commands.title: Scan Replay Folder
commands.description: Scan the configured Replay Folder and add replay files that are not already in the Catalog.

commands.title: Show Replay Leaderboard
commands.description: Show replay playback activity.

commands.title: Create Kick Clip
commands.description: Request a Kick clip through the KickBot workflow. Kick chat only.

commands.title: Create Twitch Clip
commands.description: Create a Twitch clip. Twitch chat only. Duration is 5-60 seconds.

commands.title: Create YouTube Clip
commands.description: Create a timestamped clip from the current YouTube live broadcast. YouTube chat only.

commands.title: Save Replay
commands.description: Tell OBS to save the current Replay Buffer. What happens next depends on Replay Source and Playlist settings.

commands.title: Overlay Message
commands.description: Send a message directly to the RTS overlay using the configured Message Behaviour.

commands.title: Playback History
commands.description: Show the most recently played replays.

commands.title: Screen Position
commands.description: Move the player to a saved position. Use the saved position tag, not the display name.

commands.title: Hide Player
commands.description: Hide the current player without deleting or resetting the replay.

commands.title: Pause
commands.description: Pause the current video.

commands.title: Play
commands.description: Resume the current video.

commands.title: Set Speed
commands.description: Change playback speed. Accepted range is 0.25 to 4.0.

commands.title: Show Player
commands.description: Show the current player and resume the current video.

commands.title: Playlist
commands.description: The Playlist is the live playback queue and is separate from the Catalog and playback history.

commands.title: List Playlist
commands.description: Show the current Playlist.

commands.title: Play Replay
commands.description: Add a replay to the Playlist. A replay can be selected by Catalog/search result number, custom title, or platform and user search context.

commands.title: Playlist - Clear
commands.description: Remove waiting items while leaving the currently playing item alone.

commands.title: Playlist - Clear All
commands.description: Remove everything from the Playlist without stopping a replay already playing.

commands.title: Playlist - Pause
commands.description: Pause automatic Playlist progression without stopping the current video.

commands.title: Playlist - Remove
commands.description: Remove a waiting item by its Playlist position. The currently playing item cannot be removed.

commands.title: Playlist - Resume
commands.description: Resume Playlist progression. If nothing is playing and queued items exist, Resume starts the next item.
